# Data products and access {#sec-data-products}


::: {.cell}

:::


CARS releases its data as a family of products at different levels of detail.
Choose the least detailed product that answers your question: the aggregate
tables are much easier to work with, and have already dealt with several of
the pitfalls described in @sec-pitfalls.

| Product | Unit | Format | Size | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Aggregate tables** | Postcode area × year × vehicle characteristics | CSV | KB to a few MB each | Spreadsheet users; maps; trends; comparisons between areas |
| **Vehicle table** | One row per vehicle, with one column per year | Parquet | about 9 GB | Custom groupings; cohorts; individual makes and models; anything the tables do not cover |
| **Reports and quality tables** | Documentation | Markdown, CSV | Small | Understanding how each table was made and how complete it is |

## Aggregate tables

The aggregate tables count vehicles and sum their mileage by postcode area
and year, broken down by body type, fuel, age, engine size and other
characteristics. There are four families, described in
@sec-aggregate-tables and catalogued in @sec-table-catalogue:

- **mileage tables**: vehicles and annual mileage by postcode area, year, body
  type and fuel;
- **fleet profile tables**: the make-up of the fleet by year, body type and
  age band;
- **car size and model tables**: the size, mass, CO~2~ and SUV share of the
  cars in each year and postcode area, from the RACF car fleet;
- **churn tables**: how the vehicles in each postcode area change from year to
  year as vehicles arrive, move, age and leave.

Vehicles that cannot be located in a year are included in the tables under
the statuses `unknown`, `dead` and `unborn`, so totals can be reconciled.

## The vehicle table

`vehicles_enhanced.parquet` has one row for each of the
93.4 million vehicles in scope, and 272 columns, including
21 years each of mileage, plausibility flag and postcode area. It is described
in @sec-vehicle-table, and every column is listed in the [data dictionary](dictionary/index.qmd).

## The linked source table

The linked and annualised table (@sec-sources-linkage), from
which the vehicle table is built, holds every vehicle in the DVSA download,
including those that left the roads before 2005.

## Licensing and conditions of use

The sources are published under the Open Government Licence v3.0, which
permits combining and republishing them, and the CARS products are released on
the same basis.

### Registration numbers and personal data

The vehicle table includes each vehicle's registration number, because it is
the key for linking to other data. A registration number is not in itself
personal information, and all the sources are published openly. However, a
registration number can in some circumstances be linked to a person, and so
can be personal data under data protection law.

The project's approach is that if a way to re-identify individuals from the
data is found, the project will:

1. tell the data owners;
2. store the data at a level of security suitable for the sensitivity
   discovered;
3. make the data and code available only at a suitable level of safeguarding,
   following the tiered access used by the UK Data Service.

Users must not attempt to identify individuals or their vehicles' keepers from
the data.

## Versions

The data will be revised as the method improves and new MOT data is added.
Each build of the pipeline records its versions in `session_info.csv`, and this
book states the build it describes in its preface.

::: {.callout-important title="Pitfall: vehicle_id changes between versions"}
`vehicle_id` is the row number in the input file and changes whenever a new
delivery is processed. To match vehicles across versions, or to other data,
use `registration_DVSA`.
:::
